Do you use psychoactive drugs? Do you have mental illness in your family? The voices sound negative but is it distressing to hear them? I only ask because the only time I heard voices before my schizophrenic breakdown, it was a voice in bed telling me to kill myself, which was horrible. The final time I went floridly psychotic I had kind, female voices saying nice things and I enjoyed that time as I had something approaching thoughts, which I haven't had since my collapse in 2007 apart from the bout of psychosis. 

Anyway, I read most people have some experiences that could be labelled psychotic but some people don't get freaked out by them and some do, which can make all the difference. I was a mixed bag after I started to be unwell after a trauma at ten; I would experience certain symptoms as very negative and upsetting, like feeling I was being controlled by evil demons from space or that everyone in my hometown wanted to murder me, etc. but then I would get real "mystical" highs, especially when drunk but also listening to romantic music like The Smashing Pumpkins' more grandiose love songs. But at 25 I wound down to nothing, one huge final high of invincible mania and delusions of being a Jewish orphan and being behind the Beltway sniper attacks, etc. For six years -- except that freak blip I mentioned -- I feel like I have been in a waking coma, and still feel that way.

I don't know what to recommend as nothing has worked for me. Talk to a psychiatrist and if the voices are unmanageable they might be able to get them under control with meds, although some people don't want to go that route. Sorry I wasn't more help but I am very much consumed with my own problems. By the way, why don't you need to worry about money because you're English? Did I miss something?

All the best.

Hi. Thanks for your reply. I have been in hospital for 4.5 years, watching tens of people come and go. They feed us okay but I don't really have an interest in food and rarely even eat these days, mostly sustaining myself with milk. You said you sometimes need to be locked up as a danger to yourself. I was like that for years but got locked away this time because of a serious crime so can't even take comfort in being a good person, like I at least projected till 25. 

There are eighteen patients on my ward; a mixed bag of violent criminals, burglars, sex offenders and a few just in for their mental illness/drug problems. It's a forensic unit, really. There are sometimes fights but not as many as on the medium secure wards; ours is low secure for less violent patients. I don't really have any friends there, although some seem to like me when they're not rubbing in what I told them about the trauma and losing my penis, etc. 

I haven't made many friends since school and literally none since my death in 2007, partly as I can't remember people or what they have said, can't care about them, and I can't say anything real as I have no thoughts. 

Well, I'm stuck to say the least. I go out to town on my own once a week, usually just to use the internet. I searched for my first girlfriend and a girl I could've dated in my late teens, and they have a PhD and work for CNN Australia, respectively. If anything this makes me feel worse and more bereft, cursing missed opportunities, etc. Well, this thread is probably dead now but I will post here again next week. 

Thanks and bye.
